title: Fixed affine additive coefficient column augmentations are quasi-isomorphisms
statement: Let X be separated and U a finite family of opens whose positive tuple intersections are affine. For any injective resolution I of the additive etale structure sheaf and any Cech degree n, the map from the lifted ordinary unit Cech term A^n concentrated in resolution degree zero to the actual vertical column D.X n, constructed by fromSingle₀Equiv from additiveCechCoefficientMap and its proved vertical annihilation equation, is a quasi-isomorphism. This states only a single-column comparison, not a totalization or existence of a chain map from A to Tot(D).

source.place: Theorem 59.22.4, affine acyclicity and natural coefficient sections; Tag 01EQ, Lemma 20.11.2, beta augmentation.

proof.text: Construct the coefficient-section isomorphism in each Cech degree using preservation of products by scalar forgetting and ULift, followed by the lifted inverse of restrictFunctorΓ on each tuple product. The projection equation for this isomorphism identifies its composite with the evaluated I.ι.f 0 with the prescribed additiveCechCoefficientMap. This calculation is proved by Pi.mapIso_hom_π, piComparison_comp_π, and product projection extensionality in Lean. No finiteness, separatedness, affineness, or covering assumption is needed for this step.

Degree-n Cech evaluation preserves finite limits: identify it naturally with restriction to the discrete tuple family followed by lim. Compose it with sheaf-to-presheaf and restriction along the open inclusion. Map I.isLimitKernelFork through this left exact functor, then transport the resulting kernel fork across the preceding coefficient-section isomorphism. Thus the fixed augmentation is a mono and exact with the next vertical differential. CochainComplex.quasiIsoAt₀_iff and ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_of_zeros give quasi-isomorphism in degree zero. This entire step is proved in Lean.

Use exists_etaleTensorUnit_sections_natural to obtain natural additive unit tensor-section coordinates. A generic coordinate isomorphism, proved directly from those coordinates, identifies the lifted tensor-section sheaf with X.etaleAdditiveSheaf. Apply the finite-affine Cech vanishing theorem for the unit to the finite affine etale basis, and then the Cech vanishing criterion. Transport the resulting positive derived-evaluation vanishing along the coordinate sheaf isomorphism. All coordinate constructions and this application are proved in Lean.

The intersection hypothesis with k=0 and a constant tuple gives that each U j is affine. The additive open inclusion followed by forgetting is definitionally the restriction functor. Apply etale_affineOpenCech_resolution_columns with the preceding derived-evaluation vanishing to obtain zero positive homology of every vertical column. The single-degree source is exact at every positive degree; quasiIsoAt_iff_exactAt now gives the remaining degrees. Assemble the degree-zero and positive-degree cases with the QuasiIso constructor. This uses no covering hypothesis and includes the empty tuple family.

proof_origin.place: Affine Cech acyclicity; Tag 01EQ, fixed beta column augmentation. Degree-zero kernel transport and positive-degree assembly proved in Lean using existing project declarations.

lean.statement:
theorem additiveCechCoefficientMap_column_quasiIso
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [X.IsSeparated] {ι : Type u} [Finite ι]
    (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (hU : ∀ (k : ℕ) (y : Fin (k + 1) → ι), IsAffineOpen (⨅ l, U (y l)))
    (I : InjectiveResolution X.etaleAdditiveSheaf) (n : ℕ) :
    QuasiIso
      ((CochainComplex.fromSingle₀Equiv
        ((etaleOpenCechResolutionDoubleComplex X (additiveCechOpenInclusion X) U I).X n)
        ((additiveCechCoefficientComplex U).X n)).symm
          ⟨additiveCechCoefficientMap U I n, additiveCechCoefficientMap_vertical U I n⟩)
